title: ORDER BY ASC puts BLANK before negative numbers
query: EVALUATE Nums ORDER BY Nums[N] ASC

source.supports: ASC is the default and sorts ascending; the page does not say where BLANK goes

source.quote: Blank evaluates to zero when performing a comparison
source.supports: in a comparison BLANK counts as zero (or the empty string, or FALSE)

derivation: Nums[N] by Id: -5 (1), BLANK (2), 3 (3), -1 (4), 10 (5). BLANK is taken as lower than every number, so ascending order is BLANK, -5, -1, 3, 10: Ids 2, 1, 4, 3, 5.
alternative: No source states where ORDER BY puts BLANK. Comparison operators treat BLANK as 0; if the sort does too, the order is -5, -1, BLANK, 3, 10: Ids 1, 4, 2, 3, 5.
